Subject: Request: AI risk & compliance mapping for Greenfield Health — NIST & EU AI Act

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for taking this — Greenfield Health is compiling a formal RFP addendum focused on model risk and governance. Two asks to help our procurement and legal teams move to the next stage:

1) A mapping document that shows how Redwood aligns to NIST AI RMF core functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, and Protect) with descriptions and evidence pointers (reports, logs, SOC2 controls).
2) A short position paper on how Redwood interprets the EU AI Act obligations for high-risk healthcare decision-support models, and what runtime controls / mitigations you would offer for customers in-scope (data residency, human oversight patterns, and logging/auditability).

Additional asks:
- A list of your standard evaluation / regression testing approach (how you track quality drift, test prompts, thresholding, and rollback).
- Any documentation showing encryption/key management and retention policies relevant for audit.

Could you share a draft mapping and a proposed timeline by early next week? We have counsel involved (Ben Owens at LawBridge) and they will review the wording for indemnities and classification.

Attached: our RFP addendum (GFH_AI_Risk_Addendum.pdf) for context.

Best,
Laura

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear scope. We can absolutely provide a mapping and a short position paper that covers the EU AI Act interpretation for healthcare use-cases plus our evaluation/regression approach.

Deliverables we propose:
- 'Redwood AI Risk Summary' (executive mapping to NIST AI RMF with evidence links) — attached.
- NIST mapping spreadsheet (detailed control crosswalk) — will attach in follow-up.
- EU AI Act Positioning (document outlining obligations, customer vs Redwood responsibilities, recommended contractual language).
- Evaluation & Regression brief (how we test for quality drift, metrics we track, and the rollback / canary policy).

Proposed timeline:
- Draft packet to you by EOD 2027-04-10
- Internal review with your counsel week of 2027-04-12
- Finalized mapping and optional workshop the week of 2027-04-19

If that timeline works I will route the spreadsheets and positioning note for internal redlines and send the formal package.

High-level clarifications up-front:
- Redwood provides runtime logging (token-level request/response), configurable retention windows, and customer-managed key options for Private deployments.
- For Hosted customers we offer pseudonymization and tenant isolation; for regulated customers we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.
- We do not hold PHI on behalf of customers unless a prior data processing addendum (DPA) with specific controls is executed.

Attaching: Redwood_AI_Risk_Summary_20270410.pdf (executive mapping). We will follow with a technical appendix and our NIST mapping spreadsheet.

Would you prefer a short (30-45m) technical walkthrough or a single consolidated packet?

Thanks,
Evelyn

Evelyn — forwarding internal notes below (quick replies inline quoted):

> "High-level clarifications up-front: Redwood provides runtime logging (token-level request/response), configurable retention windows, and customer-managed key options for Private deployments."

Agree — add explicit guidance for retention defaults (30/90/365) and the exact log fields we capture (timestamp, request id, model id, prompt hash, response hash, token counts). Counsel will want that enumerated.

Key points to add to the packet:
- NIST mapping sheet (attached) should include control references and example evidence artifacts (SOC2 section, sample audit log export, audit trace IDs).
- EU AI Act: include a short table mapping obligations to operational controls we offer and customer responsibilities. For healthcare high-risk, emphasize: human oversight patterns, documentation for datasets used in any fine-tuning, and model evaluation under representative clinical prompts.
- Evaluation/regression: propose a 3-tier harness: unit prompt tests (smoke), periodic prompt-sample sweep (daily/weekly depending on volume), and full regression on model changes / quantization changes with baseline diffs (precision/recall/ROUGE-like metrics + embedding drift). Must include rollback thresholds and canary percentages.

Action items (assigned):
- Neha: finalize NIST_Mapping_Table_20270410.xlsx (add evidence pointers) — ETA 2027-04-09 17:00 ET.
- Karthik: draft EU-AI-Act-Positioning_20270410.docx with recommended contractual statements for high-risk healthcare — ETA 2027-04-09 18:00 ET.
- Evelyn: assemble final packet and send to Laura / Ben with proposed review dates.

Also: Ben Owens (counsel) may ask for indemnity language adjustments — ready to coordinate.

-Neha

Highlights:
- Logging & audit: we capture request_id, model_id, timestamp, prompt hash, response hash, token counts, latency; default retention 90 days for Hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS option available in Private; HSM integrations supported for Dedicated.
